standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the degreewise action on the localised terms of the complex.

core_obligations: Represent the object: the proof chooses generators of the ideal and recalls that the local cohomology is computed by the displayed Cech complex built from the localisations of the ring (proof lines 4190-4196)

Extend the derivation: the proof uses that a derivation extends uniquely to an additive operator on every localisation, still satisfying the Leibniz rule with respect to the same derivation (proof lines 4198-4200)

Assemble the operator: the extensions act degreewise on the terms of the complex, giving the canonical additive operator on the local cohomology modules satisfying the Leibniz rule, which is the statement (proof line 4200)
proof_roadmap: 取 I = (f_1,…,f_r)，用 Čech 复形 A → ∏ A_{f_{i_0}} → … → A_{f_1…f_r} 计算 RΓ_Z(A)。
θ 唯一地延拓为各局部化上的加性算子并保持 Leibniz 法则，于是逐项作用到该复形上，得到 H^i_Z(A) 上满足 Leibniz 法则的典范加性算子 D。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement produces, for every derivation of the ring, a canonical additive operator on the local cohomology modules of a finitely generated ideal satisfying the Leibniz rule with respect to that derivation (author lemma at source lines 4180-4187, label lemma-derivation). The proof (source lines 4189-4201) is short but constructive: it represents the local cohomology by the Cech complex of the chosen generators, uses the unique extension of the derivation to each localisation appearing in the complex, and lets the extensions act degreewise. The point is that the action is canonical and compatible with the Leibniz rule, and both facts come from the explicit complex rather than from a functoriality statement. H2.
